Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: The CNIBE enables digital authentication. DPI Map records: 'Enables authentication: YES.' The card contains a microprocessor with cryptographic certificates for both authentication and electronic signatures (Scribd/Gemalto document). The Ministry of Interior launched an interactive portal enabling citizens to read data stored in their card's smart chip using a secure card reader. The November 2025 draft law on digital identity and trust services explicitly builds on the existing biometric card to enable broader digital authentication across services.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Individuals can access data stored on their CNIBE chip. The Ministry of Interior launched an interactive portal enabling users to read the data stored in their card's smart chip using a secure card reader (confirmed in the imcra-az.org digital transformation paper). Citizens can track their biometric document application status online. However, no evidence of a comprehensive self-service portal showing full database records or audit logs of data access was found. Data subject rights (access, rectification) are established under Law 18-07.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: DPI Map records: 'Enables KYC: YES.' The CNIBE (Algerian National Identity Card) is the primary document for KYC compliance under Law No. 05-01 (2005, updated 2015) on anti-money laundering. Financial institutions are required to verify identity using the National Identity Card, passport, or driver's license. KYC requirements are enforced by the Bank of Algeria and CTRF (Financial Intelligence Processing Unit). Multiple KYC compliance providers explicitly state the Algerian National Identity Card is the core KYC document. The card's NFC chip enables biometric KYC verification.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Algeria has a functioning administrative court system and Council of State (Conseil d'Etat) providing general judicial review of executive actions. Citizens can challenge government decisions including those of the Ministry of Interior regarding ID issuance through administrative courts. However, no ID-specific judicial mechanisms or specialized ID appeal tribunals were found. The DPI Map records 'Legally binding redress mechanism: NA'. General administrative law applies to ID-related disputes.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Full integration exists between the civil registration and identity systems. The National Automated Civil Status Register (NACSR/RNVA), established under Law No. 14-08 of 2014, is directly connected to the biometric document issuance system. The CNIBE application process draws data from the NACSR (birth certificate S-12 feeds NIN and personal data onto the card). A 'unified electronic counter for biometric documents' was deployed across all municipalities integrating NACSR with the biometric database in real-time. Citizens are exempt from resubmitting civil status documents already in the NACSR.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Algeria enacted Law No. 18-07 of 10 June 2018 on the protection of individuals in the processing of personal data (modeled on GDPR). This was significantly amended by Law No. 25-11 of 24 July 2025, adding mandatory Data Protection Officers, 5-day breach notification, Data Protection Impact Assessments, and expanded enforcement powers for the ANPDP. The 2025 amendment explicitly introduces definitions for biometric data, covering biometric data stored in the CNIBE system. The law applies to all personal data processing in Algeria.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The ANPDP (Autorité Nationale de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel) was formally established in 2023 under Law No. 18-07 of 2018. It is an independent administrative authority under the President of the Republic. The ANPDP has investigation authority, can conduct audits, issue enforcement orders suspending unlawful data processing, and impose administrative fines. Its mandate covers all personal data processing including government ID systems. Powers were expanded by Law 25-11 (July 2025). Website: anpdp.dz

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Formal legislation governs Algeria's national identity system. Key legal instruments include: Ordinance No. 70-20 of 19 February 1970 (civil status framework), Law No. 14-08 of 9 August 2014 (amended civil status law, established NACSR), and Presidential Decree No. 17-143 of 18 April 2017 (formally establishing the biometric national identity card/CNIBE). DPI Map confirms: 'ID or Civil Registry Act: YES'. A November 2025 draft law on digital identity and trust services (updating Law 15-04 of 2015 on electronic signatures) is also in the legislative pipeline.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: The CNIBE system was developed with Gemalto (now Thales) as the primary vendor for card production (confirmed: Gemalto produced Algeria's biometric e-passports and the CNIBE). Algeria has established its own national biometric processing infrastructure at the Ministry of Interior and operates the online application portal. However, the card personalization and production likely remains vendor-dependent (Gemalto/Thales). No technology transfer or full in-country capacity documentation found. Classified as partial in-country capacity.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: The CNIBE system is primarily funded through Algeria's domestic budget via the Ministry of Interior. No World Bank ID4D project funding for Algeria's national ID system was found (Algeria is an upper-middle income country and not a recipient of major ID4D donor support). No external donors or international development financing for the CNIBE system were identified in research. The system has been operational for nearly a decade, funded domestically. First issuance is free to citizens; loss/theft renewal fees exist but are minimal.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The CNIBE stores two fingerprints securely in the card's microprocessor chip (confirmed by Gemalto/Scribd document: 'Two fingerprints securely stored in the micro-processor'). A facial/biometric photo is also captured and stored. Fingerprints are required for applicants aged 12 and over; children under 12 are exempt from fingerprinting. Biometric data is stored both centrally in a national database and on the card chip. No iris scan evidence found.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: Identity records are stored fully digitally. The National Automated Civil Status Register (NACSR/RNVA), established under Law No. 14-08 of 9 August 2014, digitized all civil status records (births, marriages, deaths) from all municipalities nationwide. The biometric document database is integrated directly with the NACSR. Electronic civil status documents carry the same legal validity as paper originals (Executive Decree No. 15-315). The biometric identity card database is maintained centrally at the Ministry of Interior.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Algeria has a fully deployed national biometric identity card system: the Carte Nationale d'Identité Biométrique et Électronique (CNIBE). Managed by the Ministry of the Interior, Local Authorities and Territorial Planning. Established under Presidential Decree No. 17-143 of 18 April 2017. System is operational nationwide, accepting new registrations online (via passeport.interieur.gov.dz) and at daïras/municipalities. Issues a physical smart card with NFC chip and National Identification Number (NIN).

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: Partial interoperability exists: the biometric document issuance system is integrated with the National Automated Civil Status Register (NACSR), connecting all municipalities, consular offices, and the Ministry of Justice (Law 14-08, 2014). The CNIBE enables authentication (DPI Map: YES) and KYC across financial and telecom sectors. However, the DPI Map records 'Enables authentication via government portal: NA' and no documented cross-agency API framework was found. The November 2025 draft law on digital identity and trust services is designed to create a fuller interoperability platform but is not yet enacted.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The CNIBE is mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services. Wikipedia confirms the card 'is required for voting, opening bank accounts, and other legal procedures.' KYC regulations under Law No. 05-01 (AML/CFT, enforced by the Bank of Algeria) mandate identity verification using the National Identity Card as the primary document. The Bank of Algeria's Regulation No. 12-03 requires KYC compliance for all financial institutions. Digital verification of the Algerian National ID card is widely used by banks and fintechs.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The first issuance of the CNIBE is free of charge. The Algerian Embassy in Greece explicitly states: 'The national biometric and electronic identity card... is free of charge.' Wikipedia confirms: 'free of charge the first time.' Renewal in cases of loss, theft, or deterioration incurs a penalty fee (approximately CAD $20 in Canada, USD $15 in the US, EUR 10 in France). There is no fee for normal expiry renewal. No fee waivers or subsidies for vulnerable groups are specifically documented, as the first issuance is already free for all citizens.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: The Algerian CNIBE is recognized as a travel document in some regional contexts. Wikipedia confirms the card 'can also be used as a travel document for entry into certain neighboring countries without a passport.' Algeria is a member of the Arab Maghreb Union (AMU/UMA). The card is accepted for travel between some AMU member states. Algeria-Tunisia and Algeria-Mauritania borders are open; Algeria-Morocco border remains closed. No formal digital interoperability framework was found. This constitutes recognized use in some regional contexts rather than formal cross-border digital interoperability.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The CNIBE is mandatory for Algerian nationals at age 18. Optional/available for minors of any age (Wikipedia: 'mandatory at age 18, optional for minors'). The Embassy of Algeria in Washington confirms 'Any Algerian citizen, regardless of age, can apply for a National ID Card online after obtaining a biometric passport.' Children under 12 are exempt from biometric fingerprinting. The mandatory enrollment age of 18 places this in category >17.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: The CNIBE is mandatory for all Algerian nationals at age 18. Wikipedia confirms: 'mandatory at age 18, optional for minors.' The card is required for voting, opening bank accounts, and accessing a wide range of administrative services. Per the List of National Identity Card Policies by Country (Wikipedia), Algeria's biometric card 'is compulsory for all national citizens aged 16 and above' (though other sources confirm 18 as the mandatory threshold). Non-possession by eligible adults carries implicit administrative penalties via exclusion from essential services.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: Algeria operates the Chifa smart card system for healthcare access, launched in 2008 by Gemalto for CNAS (Caisse Nationale des Assurances Sociales). The Chifa card is the primary healthcare access credential for approximately 7 million beneficiaries. Enrollment in CNAS (and thus obtaining a Chifa card) requires the national identity card. However, the actual healthcare access credential is the Chifa card, not the CNIBE directly. Thus the national ID is accepted (required to enroll in the health system) but the Chifa card is the operational credential for service delivery.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: The CNIBE is explicitly issued to Algerian citizens only. Multiple official sources confirm the card is for 'Algerian nationals' and 'Algerian citizens.' Non-nationals (refugees, asylum seekers, foreign residents, temporary workers) are not eligible for the CNIBE. Foreign residents use separate residence documents (carte de résident). No evidence found of non-national eligibility for any category. Searched Algerian Embassy websites, consular guidance, UNHCR reports, and immigration policies.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Algeria has very high ID coverage. The 2018 World Bank ID4D dataset estimated approximately 4.73 million Algerians (out of ~42 million) were without an ID, representing roughly 89% coverage nationally. Given Algeria's upper-middle income status, mandatory ID requirement at age 18, and a fully deployed biometric system operational since ~2016, coverage for eligible adults (18+) is estimated to exceed 89%. The card is compulsory for Algerian nationals at age 18 and is required for voting, banking, and administrative services, incentivizing near-universal enrollment.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration is mandatory and requires government-issued ID in Algeria. Multiple sources confirm: 'Algeria requires national ID or passport registration for all SIM cards' and 'Algeria enforces strict identity regulations for SIM cards. You cannot buy a card anonymously.' The Regulatory Authority for Post and Electronic Communications (ARPCE) enforces these requirements. Both Algerian nationals (using CNIBE) and foreigners (using passport) must present ID to register a SIM card. Carriers maintain customer databases and provide access to authorities.
